He has turned the presidency into a grift, raking in billions of dollars through crypto deals, stock trades, and pardons-for-cash, all while Americans struggle to afford groceries, gas, and rent thanks to Trump’s idiotic economic policies and illegal war in Iran.
Republicans have — at best — remained silent through it all. At worst, far too many gladly enable this President’s worst and most dangerous impulses, refusing to stand with Democrats to protect our constituents and our Constitution.
We need to rein in corruption, hold bad actors accountable, and get back to the business of lowering costs for the American people, and to do that we need to take back both the House and Senate this November.

disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JOCELYN BENSON FOR GOVERNOR]
body:
[ stdin# ]Jocelyn Benson for Governor
I am proud
to introduce you to Michigan’s next Lieutenant Governor, Winnie Brinks!

I could not be more excited to welcome my friend Winnie into this campaign
— she is a strong leader who’s delivered real results for Michiganders in
our State Senate, and she’s dedicated to making sure we can keep building
a state that’s affordable and accessible to working families.

Above all else, Winnie and I agree on this: a strong government is one
that works for the people it serves.

That’s why I chose her as my running mate, and I know she will be an
incredible Lieutenant Governor.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13375?t=1001&akid=1817%2E181023%2E0Nv6S7 ]I’ve attached Winnie’s message below — I hope you can give it a read,
then chip in to support Winnie and me in our movement to defend Michigan
this November →

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13375?t=1002&akid=1817%2E181023%2E0Nv6S7 ]DONATE →

Let’s win this thing,

Jocelyn Benson

--------------BEGIN FORWARDED MESSAGE--------------
From: Winnie Brinks <info@jocelynbenson.com>
Date: Wednesday, August 19, 2026
Subject: I’m honored to be Jocelyn Benson’s pick for Lieutenant Governor
of Michigan.
To: dpwillis67@gmail.com

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13375?t=1003&akid=1817%2E181023%2E0Nv6S7 ][IMG]

Hi there,

It’s Winnie Brinks. I am humbled to officially announce that I am running
alongside Jocelyn Benson to be your next Lieutenant Governor.

There’s a lot of work to do from now until Election Day, and everyone here
on Team Benson-Brinks for Michigan is running full steam ahead to win big
in November and make Michigan a place where everyone can stay and thrive.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13375?t=1004&akid=1817%2E181023%2E0Nv6S7 ]I’ll tell you a little bit more about myself in a moment, but first I
have to ask: will you make a donation to our campaign today and help us
kick off the next stage of this race on the best foot possible?

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13375?t=1005&akid=1817%2E181023%2E0Nv6S7 ]DONATE →

I have to be honest: Growing up, I never
would’ve imagined I’d run for office, let alone be running to be your next
Lieutenant Governor.

I grew up on my family’s dairy farm, the daughter of two Dutch immigrants.
My first job was feeding the calves and putting up the hay. My paycheck
came in the form of a steer I could raise and sell for a profit.

My background isn’t typical of most folks representing us in Lansing, but
I think that’s a good thing.

My background taught me the importance of hard work, resilience, and
service to others. They’re lessons I’ve carried throughout my life, from
working in education to serving my community as a non-profit caseworker,
and they’re lessons I instilled in my three daughters.

Even my first run for office was anything but typical. I ran a write-in
campaign to even get on the ballot because my neighbors needed a voice
fighting for them, not corporations and mega-donors.

Over the years, I’ve spent countless hours knocking on the doors of my
neighbors because I fundamentally believe: good government should be about
people.

As both a State Representative and State Senator — where I became the
first woman to serve as Michigan's Senate Majority Leader — I've been
proud to fight to ensure every Michigander has a voice, from investing in
public education to protecting healthcare to cutting costs and making life
more affordable for Michiganders.

I’m ready to continue the fight alongside Jocelyn Benson because we still
have a lot of work to do to protect Michigan families.

This race isn’t going to be easy. It’s shaping up to be one of the most
competitive gubernatorial races in the country.

[ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/13375?t=1006&akid=1817%2E181023%2E0Nv6S7 ]We need all hands on deck to make sure we hit the ground running in
this next stage of the campaign, so can we count on you to rush a donation
today and help us win in November?

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

[**This is a five-alarm fire for our public lands. Will you chip in $10, $25, or $100 today to our rapid-response war chest to help us fight this massive corporate land grab?**](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/rTC_ZTKUbD6UzpHQB_3xDQ~~/AAUS1hA~/-Db8KMjTRc593vSj-xkyShY7LNgTQNda7oIIzDmC55AQ-y7GUqECk44MP31xBLFBbC6aguyE6Z5yhFGst0zL4BOobdE2i20KKvIC6a2X2AxeS7TsVj_9RbyGQheAOiw1zDoF7Q-9UW2Ps33q6KAGYK-Q6G9f9nVHT9c0AGbSeL_VWVZM2cx5CRjZrj5-vKpdUCRpVDz3bZ7LKB0dKYKJJt57a8RUJgrqwIMCJomylhczUgaTL6VaLMbv3f4rE3dI) **[**DONATE »** ](https://go.sparkpostmail1.com/f/a/rTC_ZTKUbD6UzpHQB_3xDQ~~/AAUS1hA~/-Db8KMjTRc593vSj-xkyShY7LNgTQNda7oIIzDmC55AQ-y7GUqECk44MP31xBLFBbC6aguyE6Z5yhFGst0zL4BOobdE2i20KKvIC6a2X2AxeS7TsVj_9RbyGQheAOiw1zDoF7Q-9UW2Ps33q6KAGYK-Q6G9f9nVHT9c0AGbSeL_VWVZM2cx5CRjZrj5-vKpdUCRpVDz3bZ7LKB0dKYKJJt57a8RUJgrqwIMCJomylhczUgaTL6VaLMbv3f4rE3dI) ** The administration's own proclamation stated that new mining claims wouldn't even be legally allowed until September 11th. But executives like Kyle Kimmerle—who previously sued to shrink the monument because it "locked up" his minerals—filed seven claims the very next day. **They are so eager to bulldoze ancient cliff dwellings and pristine desert landscapes for a uranium mine that they are jumping the gun on their own backdoor deal.** They are testing the waters. body:
| | [ ](http://clicksp.shawnharrisforcongress.com/f/a/z0AIYKaBD6LxN41AuanM-A~~/AAPPABA~/hb7J5bnrrTSCWFkL-Q2LLQZTw_yviYsEiA6WeGdK1Zd4Rr5t48Ofmo3-RIlMKHk8MExWW1e9EuVe8z4IUg8hKbQAJxbjoPuJZr2fLbc-eThcWGbxA2gE-ERc_f5ndK3pYoYrClwVj0vd3CLpS8ucT39w_bTZdChT3nwgW5amG6HUOWCo2PersEAmaM67mOjlLDIqRJniGIYaYNz7W5vE-KtFLAIvDNgYccy10WEQ9MeHX3PggEOEUmBOKTElqX7fMhOl1WGtL3HLtgp-40kDq1lFXz2X2laL2sh8CXDEi6JS4BaoJv3fVESLYAzMMfCk)
---
When I got off active duty and came back home to the great state of Georgia, I quickly realized that despite having thousands of service members in our communities, **_Georgia is not a veteran-friendly state,_** between state taxes on military retirement and a healthcare system that treats veterans like an afterthought.
---
| [ ](http://clicksp.shawnharrisforcongress.com/f/a/z0AIYKaBD6LxN41AuanM-A~~/AAPPABA~/hb7J5bnrrTSCWFkL-Q2LLQZTw_yviYsEiA6WeGdK1Zd4Rr5t48Ofmo3-RIlMKHk8MExWW1e9EuVe8z4IUg8hKbQAJxbjoPuJZr2fLbc-eThcWGbxA2gE-ERc_f5ndK3pYoYrClwVj0vd3CLpS8ucT39w_bTZdChT3nwgW5amG6HUOWCo2PersEAmaM67mOjlLDIqRJniGIYaYNz7W5vE-KtFLAIvDNgYccy10WEQ9MeHX3PggEOEUmBOKTElqX7fMhOl1WGtL3HLtgp-40kDq1lFXz2X2laL2sh8CXDEi6JS4BaoJv3fVESLYAzMMfCk)
---
My last assignment was in Israel. I went from leading troops in high-stakes environments to coming back home and experiencing the sudden crash that so many service members face when transitioning back to civilian life. I knew I needed help, so I called Fort Benning. They directed me to a local mental health facility. I pulled up to that clinic as General Shawn Harris. I walked to the counter, and the receptionist looked right at me and said: _"We don't take TRICARE anymore."_ I had served 40 years. I had the rank, and I had the phone numbers to call people high up in the chain of command to fix my situation. But what if I was an E-4? If a young Specialist walked into that clinic without a star on their shoulder or a direct line to a general, they would have been turned away with nowhere to go. Without help, they could have ended up dead. I walked back out, sat in my car, and thought: **_This is why I 'm getting into politics._** **My blood boils when politicians like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth treat our military like a political backdrop or talk about veterans' benefits as something to slash and privatize.** Pete Hegseth and the political class in Washington love to wrap themselves in the flag, but when our service members come home broken, struggling, or needing care, they look the other way. They treat the men and women who put their lives on the line like line items on a spreadsheet instead of human beings who earned their care. Our troops and veterans don't need political posturing or lectures on culture wars from political appointees--they need a healthcare system that actually answers the phone when they call for help. I fought for this country for four decades, and I'm not going to sit quietly while politicians neglect the men and women who served alongside me. clean_body: | | When I got off active duty and came back home to the great state of Georgia, I quickly realized that despite having thousands of service members in our communities, Georgia is not a veteran-friendly state, between state taxes on military retirement and a healthcare system that treats veterans like an afterthought. | My last assignment was in Israel. I went from leading troops in high-stakes environments to coming back home and experiencing the sudden crash that so many service members face when transitioning back to civilian life. I knew I needed help, so I called Fort Benning. They directed me to a local mental health facility. I pulled up to that clinic as General Shawn Harris. I walked to the counter, and the receptionist looked right at me and said: "We don't take TRICARE anymore." I had served 40 years. I had the rank, and I had the phone numbers to call people high up in the chain of command to fix my situation. But what if I was an E-4? If a young Specialist walked into that clinic without a star on their shoulder or a direct line to a general, they would have been turned away with nowhere to go. Without help, they could have ended up dead. I walked back out, sat in my car, and thought: This is why I 'm getting into politics. My blood boils when politicians like Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth treat our military like a political backdrop or talk about veterans' benefits as something to slash and privatize. Pete Hegseth and the political class in Washington love to wrap themselves in the flag, but when our service members come home broken, struggling, or needing care, they look the other way. They treat the men and women who put their lives on the line like line items on a spreadsheet instead of human beings who earned their care. Our troops and veterans don't need political posturing or lectures on culture wars from political appointees--they need a healthcare system that actually answers the phone when they call for help. I fought for this country for four decades, and I'm not going to sit quietly while politicians neglect the men and women who served alongside me. ~~ ~~ Thank you, Ret. Brigadier General Shawn Harris | ~~ "Facebook" ~ "X" \[BLUESKY\] "Bluesky" PAID FOR BY SHAWN FOR GEORGIA

**Thursday, August 20, 2026 -**_** ** Fifty Bodies recovered in Gaza City. Report: 94% of households in Gaza need shelter aid. Human Rights Watch: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023. Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project, cutting northern West Bank from south. Israeli settlers injure nine Palestinians as attacks continue across occupied West Bank. World Central Kitchen condemns Israeli decision to close probe into killing of its workers in Gaza. President Donald Trump calls for "economic D-Day against Iran"; Iran calls it diversion from U.S. debt crisis. U.S. officials make dubious claims about Hormuz traffic. Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules. Ansarallah claims "comprehensive blockade" of Saudi tankers. Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon. Lebanese Parliament speaker "guarantees" U.S. that Lebanese Army can assert control over south if Israel withdraws. UNIFIL hands over Khardali-Litani position to Lebanese army ahead of mission's end. U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion for first time. Trump pushes crypto industry's Clarity Act with ethics concerns looming. Los Angeles prosecutor reduces felony charges against officer who recorded colleagues' bigoted remarks. Democratic-aligned "VoteVets" official also runs credit card industry lobbying front group. Florida Democratic Senate nominee Angie Nixon calls Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu a "war criminal." Syrian FM says Israel had "no justification" for bombing air base earlier this week. Ecuador's intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash. Sudan's Rapid Support Forces see additional defections, Sudanese army claims. Russian missile strikes kill 16 amid Ukrainian interceptor shortage. Poland arrests Ukrainian man over alleged Russia-linked assassination plot. North Korea tests short-range ballistic missiles after U.S.-South Korea drills are scaled back._

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.oIe6iN_aiy7_o3epvl44jM38gNfgO7uP1G8Zlx2-SkQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=212015073)
* * *
# Palestine
* **Killed and wounded in Gaza:** Over the past 24 hours, 10 Palestinians were killed and 25 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.
* The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,417 killed, with 174,360 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,283 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,248, while 813 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble.
* **Fifty Bodies recovered in Gaza City:** Gaza Civil Defense crews [recovered](https://substack.com/redirect/af89a364-6144-4460-94d4-cae70c1516f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 50 bodies from beneath the rubble of the Al-Sawafiri, Al-Batniji, Karam, Harz, and Al-Af family homes in Gaza City after three days of work, the Palestine Information Center reported on Thursday.
* The Civil Defense agency said its teams have inspected eight completely destroyed homes where around 170 Palestinians are believed to remain buried, as recovery efforts continue while Israel obstructs the entry of equipment into the strip.
* **Report: 94% of households in Gaza need shelter aid:** An estimated 1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza, or 94% of the population, need shelter and basic household assistance, according to a new [report](https://substack.com/redirect/cc6b262f-63e7-4d65-b153-17890d8a43cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Shelter Cluster, led by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC).
* The report found that nearly two-thirds of households live in tents or makeshift shelters, structures that are not designed for long-term accommodation. More than half of households in tents had already used the same tent for over a year, while more than half of tents and makeshift shelters assessed were in poor or very poor condition.
* "A shelter is not adequate simply because it has four walls or a roof," Jehan Salim, National Shelter Cluster Coordinator, said in a statement. "Ten months after the October 2025 ceasefire, most families have lived more than a year in shelters that were never designed for long-term accommodation. The materials needed to repair homes, restore basic services and provide improved shelters are still not entering Gaza at anything close to the scale required."
* **HRW: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023:** Israeli settler attacks have fully or partially [displaced](https://substack.com/redirect/0f6eb33c-410d-4c41-9d30-76b4031088c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 107 Palestinian communities, comprising some 5,900 people, across the occupied West Bank since January 2023, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said in a new report. The Israeli military expelled another 32,000 Palestinians from their homes in the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in January 2025. HRW said Israeli authorities are "arming, funding, and granting impunity" to settlers responsible for the attacks, which increasingly target Palestinians' homes, land, livestock and access to water. The group cited OCHA figures showing an average of 6.6 settler attacks resulting in casualties or property damage per day in 2026--the highest rate it has recorded--and said at least 15 Palestinians, including two children, had been killed by settlers as of July 24.
* "The Israeli government and the settlers share the same goal of maximum land and minimum Palestinians," HRW said.
* **Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project cutting northern West Bank from south:** Israel [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/fb7051d2-eb93-4072-ab42-c85422c606aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a tender for the construction of 1,234 housing units in the E1 area east of Jerusalem, advancing a settlement project that would disrupt Palestinian territorial contiguity between Ramallah, East Jerusalem and Bethlehem, The Times of Israel reported. The units are part of roughly 3,400 homes approved last August, when Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said the project would "practically erase the two-state delusion."
* The UN Secretary-General expressed "deep alarm" over the move, with his spokesperson warning that E1 would effectively "sever the connection between the northern and southern West Bank" and pose an "existential threat" to a two-state solution.
* The UK [issued](https://substack.com/redirect/354e97a9-1ef3-4d24-aff4-32f28e633ac4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an unusually sharp response, summoning Israel's charge d'affaires and demanding the government immediately retract the tender and halt settlement expansion. Britain called the move "unacceptable and destructive" and said it "will not stand back and accept the destruction of the Two-State Solution." The government also said it would announce a "comprehensive set of measures" in the coming weeks, including sanctions targeting those involved in illegal settlement expansion.
* Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar [rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/88306d0d-3913-43c2-9d44-805f554590ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the UK's condemnation, claiming Jewish people have a right to live "throughout the Land of Israel," and invoked the Balfour Declaration--a 1917 British imperial declaration backing the establishment of a Jewish national home in historic Palestine--to defend settlement in the occupied territory.
* **Israeli settlers injure nine Palestinians as attacks continue across occupied West Bank:**
* **Ramallah:** Five Palestinians were [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/57a8feae-249b-4ab0-8b4d-0606c75b39c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Thursday in a settler attack on a vehicle between Al-Mughayyir and Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, WAFA reported. Settlers attacked the vehicle, causing it to overturn, before assaulting those inside. Israeli authorities returned the body of a 17-year-old Palestinian boy, from Sinjil, after withholding it since he was killed by Israeli forces on March 17.
* **Tubas:** A Palestinian man was [injured](https://substack.com/redirect/45e52c3f-c34f-439d-81c2-6e3b91a6d734?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) after settlers attacked him while he was working in the Al-Buqaia plain in the northern Jordan Valley.
* **Hebron:** Israeli forces [transported](https://substack.com/redirect/31805baf-518c-40ee-a0f2-55b0baa0014e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) several mobile homes to the newly established "Doron" settlement outpost on Mount Tarousa, west of Hebron. Israeli forces began excavation and land-clearing work there in June after armed settlers, under army protection, erected a tent and declared the establishment of the new settlement. Doron is among 19 new settlements approved by the Israeli government last year.
* **Nablus:** Settlers continued for a 12th consecutive day to besiege several homes in Qusra, south of Nablus, under Israeli army protection. Israeli forces [raided](https://substack.com/redirect/c1a161c5-026d-4cd4-b984-c26b04880115?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Nablus city, Salem, Bazariya, Madama and Einabus, assaulting three Palestinians and detaining 10 others.
* **World Central Kitchen condemns Israeli decision to close probe into killing of its workers in Gaza:** World Central Kitchen (WCK) condemned the Israeli military's decision to close investigations into the April 2024 strikes that killed seven of its workers. The army said Wednesday it reviewed 150 incidents of troop conduct in Gaza and only made decisions on five cases. It also closed investigations into two separate incidents that killed four Doctors Without Borders (MSF) employees in 2023 and 2024. At least 550 aid workers have been killed by Israel in Gaza since October 2023, almost all of them Palestinians.
* WCK said there was "never any excuse or justification" for the successive Israeli strikes on its clearly marked vehicles and accused the military investigation of muddying the events and shifting blame for the Israeli military's conduct. The organization renewed its demand for an independent investigation, saying the Israeli military "cannot credibly investigate its own conduct."
* Australia also [condemned](https://substack.com/redirect/c8094d4b-f9e7-41b0-bd12-a7c38e225c83?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the decision, saying it was "outraged" that Israel would not pursue criminal proceedings over the killing of Australian WCK worker Zomi Frankcom and her six colleagues, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong announcing that Israel's ambassador would be called in.
* Israeli human rights group B'Tselem called Israel's rare internal investigations a "sham" that amount to a "a legal Iron Dome to protect Israeli soldiers from potential international legal consequences."
* **Netanyahu 's rival threatens strikes on Iran as candidates compete over who would wage more war: **Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett [said](https://substack.com/redirect/6a38718b-29f8-43d3-82a1-24386a89c749?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday that, if he led the Israeli government, he would strike Iran in response to any attack by Hezbollah, claiming he would overhaul Israel's security doctrine in the role.
* Bennett, one of Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rivals ahead of Israel's October election, served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022.

# Iran
* **Trump calls for "economic D-Day against Iran"; Iran calls it diversion from U.S. debt crisis: **President Donald Trump [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/da091e5b-c2ed-4e71-8cd2-cb1502bc9b09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he was about to undertake what he called "the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country" against Iran on Wednesday, vowing "economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale," in a post on his Truth Social platform.
* Trump threatened that "any country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face tremendous economic consequences." He cited as examples of support "oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, [and] front companies."
* The warning indicates that Trump will impose additional sanctions on states and firms that keep trading with Tehran. As of Wednesday, no specific measures had been published by the Treasury Department, whose last Iran sanctions were announced on August 7.
* Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed Trump's campaign against Iran as a diversion from America's own crisis of "unprecedented debt" and surging interest costs. "Doubling down on failed policies will only bring further defeat--and enmity of Iranians," Araghchi wrote in a [post](https://substack.com/redirect/a1dfc1e1-98bc-4a9d-8378-3bbd6dcb0f08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on X Thursday, sharing CNN and New York Times reports on the U.S. national debt surpassing a record $40 trillion and rising borrowing costs, adding that U.S. "economic terrorism threatens global economy and sovereignty worldwide."
* **U.S. officials make dubious claims about Hormuz traffic:** Two U.S. officials told Axios on Wednesday that the U.S. military has been running a corridor through the Strait of Hormuz for weeks, moving about 10 million barrels of oil a day, roughly half pre-war volume, out of the Gulf via a southern channel off Oman.
* President Trump has said that "a tremendous amount of oil" is now leaving the strait and that the U.S. is not negotiating with Iran.
* Several energy analysts have [questioned](https://substack.com/redirect/8450395b-0496-477f-8e1c-9415ffe9c360?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the 10 million figure, with Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group saying available data doesn't corroborate it, and estimating flows at "at least 5-6 million bpd." Rory Johnston suggested flows nearer to 5 million bpd, calling the 10 million figure a "stretch."

* **Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules:** Iraq has [asked](https://substack.com/redirect/c2a45606-8c8b-49ef-a9ff-8fe342e6514d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Iran to grant its oil exports "special consideration" through the Strait of Hormuz, as disruptions to Gulf shipping continue to constrain Iraqi crude, Al-Monitor and the Iraqi News Agency reported on Wednesday.
* Iraqi Parliament Speaker Haibat Al-Halbousi made the request in talks with his Iranian counterpart Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Baghdad on Wednesday, saying Iraq was among the countries most affected by the regional crisis.
* Ghalibaf, who said Tuesday the strait would stay closed until the U.S. lifts its blockade, was in Iraq as part of a three-day visit to the country.

# Yemen
* **Ansarallah claims "comprehensive blockade" of Saudi tankers: **A spokesperson for Yemen's Ansarallah [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/596bbcc9-6e2c-46cc-9ae9-97d14b4b9844?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that the group had imposed a "comprehensive blockade" on Saudi ships, as part of its "siege for siege policy, " arguing that its military strength had allowed it to more effectively deter Saudi attacks.
* The spokesman said the group had targeted eight Saudi oil tankers since its blockade began, five in the Red Sea and three in the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea, and turned back 48 others.
* In response to Saudi strikes on Sanaa airport and Hodeidah port, and airspace violations over Saada and Hajjah, the spokesman said the group carried out nine operations against Yanbu, Najran, Jizan, Abha, and Eastern Province oil facilities, and 14 more targeting Saudi forces at sites including Marib and al-Makha.

# Lebanon
* **Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon:** Israel continued its attacks across southern Lebanon on Thursday, carrying out a large explosion near Zawtar Al-Sharqieh in Nabatieh governorate, while renewed Israeli shelling [struck](https://substack.com/redirect/e2c01059-9ce5-46d5-a1a3-506abf032e5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Houla and the area between Talloussa and Markaba, also in Nabatieh governorate, according to Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA).
* Heavy Israeli artillery fire [targeted](https://substack.com/redirect/fd5c1475-7f58-405d-803a-5377b20b25b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wadi Al-Salouqi, Wadi Al-Hujeir and valleys around Qabrikha and Touline, spanning Nabatieh and Bint Jbeil districts. In Tyre (Sour) governorate, Israeli forces carried out an explosion in the town of Mansouri.
* On Wednesday, Israeli forces [carried out ](https://substack.com/redirect/84f56360-437c-4b98-8e7d-0f840de203bd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)a wave of attacks and demolitions, striking Mansouri from the air, shelling Srebbine and blowing up homes in Zawtar Sharqieh, Tallouseh, Bani Hayyan, Houla and Khiam. In Mansouri, Israeli forces demolished and burned homes before renewed airstrikes later in the day.
* **Parliament speaker "guarantees" U.S. that Lebanese Army can assert control over south if Israel withdraws:** Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri [said](https://substack.com/redirect/fb4ac841-a6bd-407e-8279-691436776929?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday that the situation in southern Lebanon has become "unbearable" and is comparable to Gaza in the scale of Israel's destruction, killings, and attacks on homes and heritage, L'Orient Today reported.
* Speaking to a delegation from the American Task Force on Lebanon (ATFL), Berri said the U.S. and President Trump were uniquely positioned to force Israel to end the war and withdraw to the international border.
* If Israel withdraws, Berri, Hezbollah's chief political ally, said he would "guarantee the immediate deployment of the Lebanese Army" throughout the area south of the Litani River, with the army becoming the sole armed force responsible for security there.
* Separately on Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron [invited](https://substack.com/redirect/0878e2ef-cabb-4540-a6aa-5cdcc6c68ad7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Lebanese government to a September 17 preparatory meeting in Paris ahead of an international conference aimed at supporting the Lebanese Army and Internal Security Forces. The conference, originally expected in March, was postponed following the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Israel's escalation of its war on Lebanon.
* **UNIFIL hands over Khardali-Litani position to Lebanese army ahead of mission 's end: **The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), the UN peacekeeping mission deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978, [handed over](https://substack.com/redirect/4797c0ff-b1fd-4160-aa17-4765fd79e3f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) its position near the Lebanese army post in the Khardali-Litani area to the army's 7th Brigade, NNA reported. The transfer is part of a plan to hand a number of UNIFIL positions to the Lebanese army ahead of the mission's scheduled termination at the end of this year.

# U.S. News
* **U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion for first time** : America's gross national debt [surpassed](https://substack.com/redirect/57b0098d-947f-4ddf-aaff-f0448d5879f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a record $40 trillion Wednesday, with the country on track to borrow more than $2 trillion this year alone amid spending on the Iran war and 2025 tax cuts. Rising interest payments now account for about half the country's annual borrowing.
* Treasury Secretary **Scott Bessent** , who set a goal of cutting the deficit to 3% of GDP by 2028, acknowledged that the deficit is moving in the wrong direction this year.
* His department unexpectedly announced on Wednesday that it would "at least double" its long-dated debt buybacks, from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, after yields on long-term government bonds surged to their highest levels in nearly two decades.
* The move, targeting 10- to 30-year debt, sent the 30-year yield down nearly 10 basis points and pushed the dollar sharply lower.

* **Trump pushes crypto industry 's Clarity Act with ethics concerns looming:** President Donald Trump [called on](https://substack.com/redirect/3e0415f1-3ff9-477f-9b8e-ec4426b432a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Congress to pass the Clarity Act, a bill establishing federal regulatory rules for digital assets, at a White House event Wednesday attended by executives from Coinbase, Ripple, and other crypto companies.
* The bill would split crypto regulatory authority between the SEC and CFTC, impose anti-money-laundering rules, and ban senior officials, including the president, from creating digital assets while in office.
* Trump held this meeting and advocated for this legislation amid concerns about his personal ties to the industry, having taken in more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency-related ventures in 2025. The Trump family's crypto business has expanded under his second term as well, with Trump's World Liberty Financial company and personal meme coins having netted the family hundreds of millions of dollars each.
* **LA prosecutor reduces felony charges against officer who recorded colleagues ' bigoted remarks:** Los Angeles County District Attorney **Nathan Hochman** [said](https://substack.com/redirect/dac351da-7321-47ec-ad59-7b7c2fe57620?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Wednesday he would reduce felony charges against LAPD officer **Daniel Flores** , who secretly recorded 16 colleagues making racist, sexist, and homophobic remarks, to misdemeanor charges.
* Hochman, who was heavily criticized for his charging decision, maintained the recordings themselves violated California's two-party consent eavesdropping law, though he called the comments themselves "abhorrent."
* Flores, who taped co-workers 122 times over about a year before filing a complaint with the police commission in January 2025, will now be eligible for judicial diversion that could leave him with no criminal record if he avoids breaking the law for a year.
* **Democratic-aligned "VoteVets" official also runs credit card industry lobbying front group**: **Peter Kauffmann** , vice chair of the Democratic-aligned veterans group VoteVets and treasurer of its philanthropic arm, also [serves](https://substack.com/redirect/414d49fd-d1b5-4423-9bf2-6d8d3f83b4d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as chief spokesperson for the Small Business Payments Alliance, a group funded by the credit card industry that fights to protect swipe fees charged by Visa and Mastercard, according to new reporting from The American Prospect.
* The Small Business Payments Alliance, a project of the credit-card-industry-funded Electronic Payment Coalition, has spent millions lobbying against the Credit Card Competition Act, and a report from Demand Progress found many of its member businesses have received funding directly from Mastercard, JPMorgan Chase, and Capital One.
* VoteVets's political action committee has separately raised more than $20 million this year from billionaire donors to intervene in Democratic primaries favoring moderate, veteran-affiliated candidates over progressives, including $10 million spent boosting Iowa state Rep. **Josh Turek** over progressive **Zach Wahls**. Read the full report [here](https://substack.com/redirect/414d49fd-d1b5-4423-9bf2-6d8d3f83b4d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* **Florida Democratic Senate nominee Nixon calls Netanyahu a "war criminal": Angie Nixon**, who won Tuesday's Democratic Senate primary in Florida, [called](https://substack.com/redirect/260fa6f4-e9ad-4bdf-91b3-96e18b526986?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Israeli Prime Minister **Benjamin Netanyahu** a "war criminal" during on "Morning Joe" on Wednesday, saying he "needs to answer for his [crimes]" and that she opposes "sending any money or weapons to Israel at this moment."
* "Right now, here in our state, in our country, we have veterans that are living unhoused on the streets," Nixon said. "We have teachers that are calling my state office monthly because they can't afford to live in the state of Florida anymore."
* Analysis of Nixon's victory [published](https://substack.com/redirect/1cfccea4-50fe-4c0c-b813-e30ba9387225?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by the Washington Post on Wednesday found that she depended on a new coalition, performing strongest in counties that were younger, poorer, less college-educated and had larger Black populations. Nixon won the least college-educated and Blackest counties by roughly 30 points, carried counties with median household incomes below $65,000 by 20 points, and dominated areas with the largest shares of young adults.

# Other International News
* **Ecuador 's intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash: **The director general of Ecuador's intelligence agency (CIES), Michele Sensi-Contugi, was among seven dead as a result of a helicopter [crash](https://substack.com/redirect/8eb7c12c-68de-4d9c-9503-b1f7a7204e97?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in central Kenya, officials said on Wednesday.
* The U.S. State Department confirmed five Americans were among the dead, including a Telemundo executive and a Miami restauranteur.
* The aircraft, carrying guests from the luxury tour operator &Beyond, crashed in the foothills of Mount Ololokwe in Samburu County. The cause of the crash remains under investigation.
* Sensi-Contugi, 42, appointed to lead Ecuador's National Intelligence Center in 2024, was a close associate of right-wing President Daniel Noboa, a key U.S. partner in Washington's militarized anti-cartel push.
* He and the CIES "served as architects of the political lawfare, police state, and brutal crackdown against journalists, indigenous members of the 2025 General Strike... and leftwing figures," Drop Site contributor Camila Lourdes Galarza writes.

* **Russian missile strikes kill 16 amid Ukrainian interceptor shortage:** Russia [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/f152dcd1-fa2e-481c-b4e9-18ced8aa7256?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a large-scale missile attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, firing dozens of cruise, ballistic and hypersonic missiles alongside 168 drones, killing at least 16 people and wounding more than 40. Ukrainian officials said 30 residential buildings, a school, children's hospital, and kindergarten were damaged, while some 90,000 households temporarily lost power.
* Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine's dwindling stock of Patriot interceptors had not been replenished and accused allies of responding inadequately.
* A separate wave of attacks also struck infrastructure in Odessa, where repeated Russian attacks on ports and shipping have sharply disrupted Ukrainian agricultural exports.

* **Poland arrests Ukrainian man over alleged Russia-linked assassination plot:** Polish authorities [arrested](https://substack.com/redirect/37e0df10-f3fd-4fb7-bc5b-9a0885cced2f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Ukrainian man accused of trying to assassinate a representative of Ukraine's arms industry in Irpin, near Kyiv, on behalf of Russian intelligence. Investigators said the suspect planted an improvised explosive device beneath the target's car that was meant to be detonated remotely by cell phone but failed because of a malfunction.
* The suspect fled to Poland after the failed attack and was arrested in Warsaw, where he faces charges including attempted murder with explosives and could receive life imprisonment.
* **RSF sees additional defections, army claims:** Sudan's army said 315 fighters from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces [defected](https://substack.com/redirect/e29c62ac-d855-4842-b6f5-ac96269d72a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday, led by Brig. Gen. Musa Khamiseen, as they crossed from North Darfur into Northern State before traveling under military intelligence escort to Omdurman, according to Sudan Tribune.
* Khamiseen's reception by the army has drawn criticism from some of its Darfuri allies, who accuse him of involvement in summary executions and civilian killings during the RSF siege and capture of El Fasher last year.
* One fighter who was present during the siege accused Khamiseen of participating in killings near the earthen barricade erected to prevent civilians from fleeing and said he was filmed alongside Al-Fateh Abu Lulu, an RSF commander notorious for recording himself carrying out summary executions.

* **North Korea tests short-range ballistic missiles after U.S.-South Korea drills are scaled back:** North Korea [launched](https://substack.com/redirect/a5e2f540-f1e7-431c-acda-8c20d80dd3d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) roughly 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area toward its eastern waters, prompting South Korea's national security council to hold an emergency meeting and call on Pyongyang to stop launches they say are prohibited by U.N. Security Council resolutions.
* The test came a day after the U.S. and South Korea announced they were reducing the size of the 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises after President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon to "substantially reduce" the drills in an apparent attempt to revive diplomacy with Kim Jong Un.
* **Syrian FM says Israel had "no justification" for bombing air base earlier this week: **Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani [told](https://substack.com/redirect/3d39209b-c170-480a-8f03-0ad61c5a279e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Axios on Wednesday that Israel had no justification for bombing the Abu al-Duhur airbase, saying Damascus had explicitly informed Israel that no Turkish base or permanent Turkish troop deployment was planned there.
* Israel dropped at least eight bombs on the site on Tuesday, damaging newly rebuilt runways and hangars.
* Al-Shaibani said the base was largely empty and being rehabilitated for Syria's air force, though Turkish officers had previously visited the site as part of broader military cooperation between the countries.

* **Drop Site dispatch from Cuba:** Amid a total oil blockade imposed by the U.S.--resulting in nationwide blackouts, medicine shortages, and disruptions to hospital operations--Cuba is transitioning away from fossil fuels toward renewable energy. Over 2,500 photovoltaic parks have been inaugurated across the country, a 96% increase over those built this time last year.**Drop Site contributor Sasi Alejandre reports from Cuba, breaking down the country 's push toward an energy revolution; watch the video [here](https://substack.com/redirect/5e3ac708-ac90-4b72-a506-21b9ec3438ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**

Human Rights Watch: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023. Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project, cutting northern West Bank from south. Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules. Ansarallah claims "comprehensive blockade" of Saudi tankers. Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Palestine Killed and wounded in Gaza: Over the past 24 hours, 10 Palestinians were killed and 25 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,417 killed, with 174,360 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,283 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 4,248, while 813 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Fifty Bodies recovered in Gaza City: Gaza Civil Defense crews 50 bodies from beneath the rubble of the Al-Sawafiri, Al-Batniji, Karam, Harz, and Al-Af family homes in Gaza City after three days of work, the Palestine Information Center reported on Thursday. The Civil Defense agency said its teams have inspected eight completely destroyed homes where around 170 Palestinians are believed to remain buried, as recovery efforts continue while Israel obstructs the entry of equipment into the strip. Report: 94% of households in Gaza need shelter aid: An estimated 1.98 million Palestinians in Gaza, or 94% of the population, need shelter and basic household assistance, according to a new by the Shelter Cluster, led by the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC). The report found that nearly two-thirds of households live in tents or makeshift shelters, structures that are not designed for long-term accommodation. More than half of households in tents had already used the same tent for over a year, while more than half of tents and makeshift shelters assessed were in poor or very poor condition. "A shelter is not adequate simply because it has four walls or a roof," Jehan Salim, National Shelter Cluster Coordinator, said in a statement. "Ten months after the October 2025 ceasefire, most families have lived more than a year in shelters that were never designed for long-term accommodation. The materials needed to repair homes, restore basic services and provide improved shelters are still not entering Gaza at anything close to the scale required." HRW: Israeli settler violence has displaced 107 West Bank communities since 2023: Israeli settler attacks have fully or partially 107 Palestinian communities, comprising some 5,900 people, across the occupied West Bank since January 2023, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said in a new report. The Israeli military expelled another 32,000 Palestinians from their homes in the Jenin, Tulkarem, and Nur Shams camps in January 2025. HRW said Israeli authorities are "arming, funding, and granting impunity" to settlers responsible for the attacks, which increasingly target Palestinians' homes, land, livestock and access to water. The group cited OCHA figures showing an average of 6.6 settler attacks resulting in casualties or property damage per day in 2026--the highest rate it has recorded--and said at least 15 Palestinians, including two children, had been killed by settlers as of July 24. "The Israeli government and the settlers share the same goal of maximum land and minimum Palestinians," HRW said. Israel opens bidding for 1,234 units within settlement project cutting northern West Bank from south: Israel a tender for the construction of 1,234 housing units in the E1 area east of Jerusalem, advancing a settlement project that would disrupt Palestinian territorial contiguity between Ramallah, East Jerusalem and Bethlehem, The Times of Israel reported. The units are part of roughly 3,400 homes approved last August, when Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich said the project would "practically erase the two-state delusion." The UN Secretary-General expressed "deep alarm" over the move, with his spokesperson warning that E1 would effectively "sever the connection between the northern and southern West Bank" and pose an "existential threat" to a two-state solution. The UK an unusually sharp response, summoning Israel's charge d'affaires and demanding the government immediately retract the tender and halt settlement expansion. Britain called the move "unacceptable and destructive" and said it "will not stand back and accept the destruction of the Two-State Solution." The government also said it would announce a "comprehensive set of measures" in the coming weeks, including sanctions targeting those involved in illegal settlement expansion. Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar the UK's condemnation, claiming Jewish people have a right to live "throughout the Land of Israel," and invoked the Balfour Declaration--a 1917 British imperial declaration backing the establishment of a Jewish national home in historic Palestine--to defend settlement in the occupied territory. Israeli settlers injure nine Palestinians as attacks continue across occupied West Bank: Ramallah: Five Palestinians were Thursday in a settler attack on a vehicle between Al-Mughayyir and Abu Falah, northeast of Ramallah, WAFA reported. Settlers attacked the vehicle, causing it to overturn, before assaulting those inside. Israeli authorities returned the body of a 17-year-old Palestinian boy, from Sinjil, after withholding it since he was killed by Israeli forces on March 17. Tubas: A Palestinian man was after settlers attacked him while he was working in the Al-Buqaia plain in the northern Jordan Valley. Hebron: Israeli forces several mobile homes to the newly established "Doron" settlement outpost on Mount Tarousa, west of Hebron. Israeli forces began excavation and land-clearing work there in June after armed settlers, under army protection, erected a tent and declared the establishment of the new settlement. Doron is among 19 new settlements approved by the Israeli government last year. Nablus: Settlers continued for a 12th consecutive day to besiege several homes in Qusra, south of Nablus, under Israeli army protection. Israeli forces Nablus city, Salem, Bazariya, Madama and Einabus, assaulting three Palestinians and detaining 10 others. World Central Kitchen condemns Israeli decision to close probe into killing of its workers in Gaza: World Central Kitchen (WCK) condemned the Israeli military's decision to close investigations into the April 2024 strikes that killed seven of its workers. The army said Wednesday it reviewed 150 incidents of troop conduct in Gaza and only made decisions on five cases. It also closed investigations into two separate incidents that killed four Doctors Without Borders (MSF) employees in 2023 and 2024. At least 550 aid workers have been killed by Israel in Gaza since October 2023, almost all of them Palestinians. WCK said there was "never any excuse or justification" for the successive Israeli strikes on its clearly marked vehicles and accused the military investigation of muddying the events and shifting blame for the Israeli military's conduct. The organization renewed its demand for an independent investigation, saying the Israeli military "cannot credibly investigate its own conduct." Australia also the decision, saying it was "outraged" that Israel would not pursue criminal proceedings over the killing of Australian WCK worker Zomi Frankcom and her six colleagues, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong announcing that Israel's ambassador would be called in. Israeli human rights group B'Tselem called Israel's rare internal investigations a "sham" that amount to a "a legal Iron Dome to protect Israeli soldiers from potential international legal consequences." Netanyahu 's rival threatens strikes on Iran as candidates compete over who would wage more war: Former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett Wednesday that, if he led the Israeli government, he would strike Iran in response to any attack by Hezbollah, claiming he would overhaul Israel's security doctrine in the role. Bennett, one of Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rivals ahead of Israel's October election, served as prime minister from 2021 to 2022. Iran Trump calls for "economic D-Day against Iran"; Iran calls it diversion from U.S. debt crisis: President Donald Trump he was about to undertake what he called "the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country" against Iran on Wednesday, vowing "economic warfare and isolation on an unprecedented scale," in a post on his Truth Social platform. Trump threatened that "any country that allows its financial institutions, businesses, airports, or government entities to provide any type of lifeline to Iran will itself face tremendous economic consequences." He cited as examples of support "oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, exchange houses, ship registries, [and] front companies." The warning indicates that Trump will impose additional sanctions on states and firms that keep trading with Tehran. As of Wednesday, no specific measures had been published by the Treasury Department, whose last Iran sanctions were announced on August 7. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed Trump's campaign against Iran as a diversion from America's own crisis of "unprecedented debt" and surging interest costs. "Doubling down on failed policies will only bring further defeat--and enmity of Iranians," Araghchi wrote in a on X Thursday, sharing CNN and New York Times reports on the U.S. national debt surpassing a record $40 trillion and rising borrowing costs, adding that U.S. "economic terrorism threatens global economy and sovereignty worldwide." U.S. officials make dubious claims about Hormuz traffic: Two U.S. officials told Axios on Wednesday that the U.S. military has been running a corridor through the Strait of Hormuz for weeks, moving about 10 million barrels of oil a day, roughly half pre-war volume, out of the Gulf via a southern channel off Oman. President Trump has said that "a tremendous amount of oil" is now leaving the strait and that the U.S. is not negotiating with Iran. Several energy analysts have the 10 million figure, with Gregory Brew of Eurasia Group saying available data doesn't corroborate it, and estimating flows at "at least 5-6 million bpd." Rory Johnston suggested flows nearer to 5 million bpd, calling the 10 million figure a "stretch." Iraq asks Iran for eased oil exporting rules: Iraq has Iran to grant its oil exports "special consideration" through the Strait of Hormuz, as disruptions to Gulf shipping continue to constrain Iraqi crude, Al-Monitor and the Iraqi News Agency reported on Wednesday. Iraqi Parliament Speaker Haibat Al-Halbousi made the request in talks with his Iranian counterpart Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf in Baghdad on Wednesday, saying Iraq was among the countries most affected by the regional crisis. Ghalibaf, who said Tuesday the strait would stay closed until the U.S. lifts its blockade, was in Iraq as part of a three-day visit to the country. Yemen Ansarallah claims "comprehensive blockade" of Saudi tankers: A spokesperson for Yemen's Ansarallah on Wednesday that the group had imposed a "comprehensive blockade" on Saudi ships, as part of its "siege for siege policy, " arguing that its military strength had allowed it to more effectively deter Saudi attacks. The spokesman said the group had targeted eight Saudi oil tankers since its blockade began, five in the Red Sea and three in the Gulf of Aden and Arabian Sea, and turned back 48 others. In response to Saudi strikes on Sanaa airport and Hodeidah port, and airspace violations over Saada and Hajjah, the spokesman said the group carried out nine operations against Yanbu, Najran, Jizan, Abha, and Eastern Province oil facilities, and 14 more targeting Saudi forces at sites including Marib and al-Makha. Lebanon Israel continues ceasefire violations with shelling and demolitions across southern Lebanon: Israel continued its attacks across southern Lebanon on Thursday, carrying out a large explosion near Zawtar Al-Sharqieh in Nabatieh governorate, while renewed Israeli shelling Houla and the area between Talloussa and Markaba, also in Nabatieh governorate, according to Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA). Heavy Israeli artillery fire Wadi Al-Salouqi, Wadi Al-Hujeir and valleys around Qabrikha and Touline, spanning Nabatieh and Bint Jbeil districts. In Tyre (Sour) governorate, Israeli forces carried out an explosion in the town of Mansouri. On Wednesday, Israeli forces wave of attacks and demolitions, striking Mansouri from the air, shelling Srebbine and blowing up homes in Zawtar Sharqieh, Tallouseh, Bani Hayyan, Houla and Khiam. In Mansouri, Israeli forces demolished and burned homes before renewed airstrikes later in the day. Parliament speaker "guarantees" U.S. that Lebanese Army can assert control over south if Israel withdraws: Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri on Wednesday that the situation in southern Lebanon has become "unbearable" and is comparable to Gaza in the scale of Israel's destruction, killings, and attacks on homes and heritage, L'Orient Today reported. Speaking to a delegation from the American Task Force on Lebanon (ATFL), Berri said the U.S. and President Trump were uniquely positioned to force Israel to end the war and withdraw to the international border. If Israel withdraws, Berri, Hezbollah's chief political ally, said he would "guarantee the immediate deployment of the Lebanese Army" throughout the area south of the Litani River, with the army becoming the sole armed force responsible for security there. Separately on Wednesday, French President Emmanuel Macron the Lebanese government to a September 17 preparatory meeting in Paris ahead of an international conference aimed at supporting the Lebanese Army and Internal Security Forces. The conference, originally expected in March, was postponed following the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and Israel's escalation of its war on Lebanon. UNIFIL hands over Khardali-Litani position to Lebanese army ahead of mission 's end: The United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), the UN peacekeeping mission deployed in southern Lebanon since 1978, its position near the Lebanese army post in the Khardali-Litani area to the army's 7th Brigade, NNA reported. The transfer is part of a plan to hand a number of UNIFIL positions to the Lebanese army ahead of the mission's scheduled termination at the end of this year. U.S. News U.S. national debt tops $40 trillion for first time : America's gross national debt a record $40 trillion Wednesday, with the country on track to borrow more than $2 trillion this year alone amid spending on the Iran war and 2025 tax cuts. Rising interest payments now account for about half the country's annual borrowing. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent , who set a goal of cutting the deficit to 3% of GDP by 2028, acknowledged that the deficit is moving in the wrong direction this year. His department unexpectedly announced on Wednesday that it would "at least double" its long-dated debt buybacks, from $2 billion to at least $4 billion per operation, after yields on long-term government bonds surged to their highest levels in nearly two decades. The move, targeting 10- to 30-year debt, sent the 30-year yield down nearly 10 basis points and pushed the dollar sharply lower. Trump pushes crypto industry 's Clarity Act with ethics concerns looming: President Donald Trump Congress to pass the Clarity Act, a bill establishing federal regulatory rules for digital assets, at a White House event Wednesday attended by executives from Coinbase, Ripple, and other crypto companies. The bill would split crypto regulatory authority between the SEC and CFTC, impose anti-money-laundering rules, and ban senior officials, including the president, from creating digital assets while in office. Trump held this meeting and advocated for this legislation amid concerns about his personal ties to the industry, having taken in more than $1.4 billion from cryptocurrency-related ventures in 2025. The Trump family's crypto business has expanded under his second term as well, with Trump's World Liberty Financial company and personal meme coins having netted the family hundreds of millions of dollars each. LA prosecutor reduces felony charges against officer who recorded colleagues ' bigoted remarks: Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman Wednesday he would reduce felony charges against LAPD officer Daniel Flores , who secretly recorded 16 colleagues making racist, sexist, and homophobic remarks, to misdemeanor charges. Hochman, who was heavily criticized for his charging decision, maintained the recordings themselves violated California's two-party consent eavesdropping law, though he called the comments themselves "abhorrent." Flores, who taped co-workers 122 times over about a year before filing a complaint with the police commission in January 2025, will now be eligible for judicial diversion that could leave him with no criminal record if he avoids breaking the law for a year. Democratic-aligned "VoteVets" official also runs credit card industry lobbying front group: Peter Kauffmann , vice chair of the Democratic-aligned veterans group VoteVets and treasurer of its philanthropic arm, also as chief spokesperson for the Small Business Payments Alliance, a group funded by the credit card industry that fights to protect swipe fees charged by Visa and Mastercard, according to new reporting from The American Prospect. The Small Business Payments Alliance, a project of the credit-card-industry-funded Electronic Payment Coalition, has spent millions lobbying against the Credit Card Competition Act, and a report from Demand Progress found many of its member businesses have received funding directly from Mastercard, JPMorgan Chase, and Capital One. VoteVets's political action committee has separately raised more than $20 million this year from billionaire donors to intervene in Democratic primaries favoring moderate, veteran-affiliated candidates over progressives, including $10 million spent boosting Iowa state Rep. Josh Turek over progressive Zach Wahls. Read the full report . Florida Democratic Senate nominee Nixon calls Netanyahu a "war criminal": Angie Nixon, who won Tuesday's Democratic Senate primary in Florida, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal" during on "Morning Joe" on Wednesday, saying he "needs to answer for his [crimes]" and that she opposes "sending any money or weapons to Israel at this moment." "Right now, here in our state, in our country, we have veterans that are living unhoused on the streets," Nixon said. "We have teachers that are calling my state office monthly because they can't afford to live in the state of Florida anymore." Analysis of Nixon's victory by the Washington Post on Wednesday found that she depended on a new coalition, performing strongest in counties that were younger, poorer, less college-educated and had larger Black populations. Nixon won the least college-educated and Blackest counties by roughly 30 points, carried counties with median household incomes below $65,000 by 20 points, and dominated areas with the largest shares of young adults. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News Ecuador 's intelligence chief and five Americans killed in Kenya helicopter crash: The director general of Ecuador's intelligence agency (CIES), Michele Sensi-Contugi, was among seven dead as a result of a helicopter in central Kenya, officials said on Wednesday. The U.S. State Department confirmed five Americans were among the dead, including a Telemundo executive and a Miami restauranteur. The aircraft, carrying guests from the luxury tour operator &Beyond, crashed in the foothills of Mount Ololokwe in Samburu County. The cause of the crash remains under investigation. Sensi-Contugi, 42, appointed to lead Ecuador's National Intelligence Center in 2024, was a close associate of right-wing President Daniel Noboa, a key U.S. partner in Washington's militarized anti-cartel push. He and the CIES "served as architects of the political lawfare, police state, and brutal crackdown against journalists, indigenous members of the 2025 General Strike... and leftwing figures," Drop Site contributor Camila Lourdes Galarza writes. Russian missile strikes kill 16 amid Ukrainian interceptor shortage: Russia a large-scale missile attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, firing dozens of cruise, ballistic and hypersonic missiles alongside 168 drones, killing at least 16 people and wounding more than 40. Ukrainian officials said 30 residential buildings, a school, children's hospital, and kindergarten were damaged, while some 90,000 households temporarily lost power. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine's dwindling stock of Patriot interceptors had not been replenished and accused allies of responding inadequately. A separate wave of attacks also struck infrastructure in Odessa, where repeated Russian attacks on ports and shipping have sharply disrupted Ukrainian agricultural exports. Poland arrests Ukrainian man over alleged Russia-linked assassination plot: Polish authorities a Ukrainian man accused of trying to assassinate a representative of Ukraine's arms industry in Irpin, near Kyiv, on behalf of Russian intelligence. Investigators said the suspect planted an improvised explosive device beneath the target's car that was meant to be detonated remotely by cell phone but failed because of a malfunction. The suspect fled to Poland after the failed attack and was arrested in Warsaw, where he faces charges including attempted murder with explosives and could receive life imprisonment. RSF sees additional defections, army claims: Sudan's army said 315 fighters from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces on Wednesday, led by Brig. Gen. Musa Khamiseen, as they crossed from North Darfur into Northern State before traveling under military intelligence escort to Omdurman, according to Sudan Tribune. Khamiseen's reception by the army has drawn criticism from some of its Darfuri allies, who accuse him of involvement in summary executions and civilian killings during the RSF siege and capture of El Fasher last year. One fighter who was present during the siege accused Khamiseen of participating in killings near the earthen barricade erected to prevent civilians from fleeing and said he was filmed alongside Al-Fateh Abu Lulu, an RSF commander notorious for recording himself carrying out summary executions. North Korea tests short-range ballistic missiles after U.S.-South Korea drills are scaled back: North Korea roughly 10 short-range ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area toward its eastern waters, prompting South Korea's national security council to hold an emergency meeting and call on Pyongyang to stop launches they say are prohibited by U.N. Security Council resolutions. The test came a day after the U.S. and South Korea announced they were reducing the size of the 11-day Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises after President Donald Trump ordered the Pentagon to "substantially reduce" the drills in an apparent attempt to revive diplomacy with Kim Jong Un. Syrian FM says Israel had "no justification" for bombing air base earlier this week: Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani Axios on Wednesday that Israel had no justification for bombing the Abu al-Duhur airbase, saying Damascus had explicitly informed Israel that no Turkish base or permanent Turkish troop deployment was planned there. Israel dropped at least eight bombs on the site on Tuesday, damaging newly rebuilt runways and hangars. Al-Shaibani said the base was largely empty and being rehabilitated for Syria's air force, though Turkish officers had previously visited the site as part of broader military cooperation between the countries. Drop Site dispatch from Cuba: Amid a total oil blockade imposed by the U.S.--resulting in nationwide blackouts, medicine shortages, and disruptions to hospital operations--Cuba is transitioning away from fossil fuels toward renewable energy. body:
#
Breaking news, Peter:
**I just signed an executive order to protect the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness (BWCAW) from the Trump administration and mining companies.**
**[If you support this, stand with me by pitching in a contribution now →](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260820-1.BJa3Nr&amount=5&refcode=em20260820-985&t=2&akid=985%2E34582%2EGpv_aO)**
The Boundary Waters is Minnesota’s greatest natural treasure, where outdoor enthusiasts and families come to canoe, hike, fish, camp, and so much more. There are countless reasons why it’s the most visited wilderness area _in the entire country_ : it offers pristine waters, abundant fish and wildlife, and a vast wilderness teeming with biodiversity.
For decades, international mining interests have set their sights on the Rainy River Headwaters Watershed, which flows into the Boundary Waters, for potential copper nickel mining.
And for decades, Minnesotans have successfully protected this sacred place for future generations — that is, until Donald Trump returned to the White House.
**The Trump administration has relentlessly attacked the BWCAW, and last April, he formally ended the mining ban on federal land that includes the Boundary Waters watershed.**
He’s trying to open up this fragile ecosystem to irreversible pollution for the sake of profits while undermining the will of the people, as 70 percent of Minnesotans want to see the Boundary Waters permanently protected.
It’s the Minnesota way to leave our pristine wilderness as we found it. That’s why I’m using my authority as governor to do just that with this executive order.
**But we know the Trump administration is going to fight this with everything they’ve got.****[So I’m asking, Peter: can I count on you to chip in $5 to help fuel our fight to preserve the Boundary Waters for generations to come?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20260820-1.BJa3Nr&amount=5&refcode=em20260820-985&t=3&akid=985%2E34582%2EGpv_aO)**

With gratitude,
Tim

Now that the primary is behind us, I want to properly reintroduce myself.
But before I do, I need you to read this:

Republicans have committed to spending $51 million on Michigan to prop up
our opponent and smear my name over the airwaves.

The only way to break through that noise is by organizing and running ads
of our own — and because this campaign is 100% people-powered, I’m
counting on your support to fuel that work. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260820-1-ak.y_M_de&amount=10&refcode=em20260820-2972&t=1004&akid=2975%2E251025%2ExgV1uk ]Can you chip in any amount
today to help us reach undecided voters before the MAGA money does?

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260820-1-ak.y_M_de&amount=10&refcode=em20260820-2972&t=1005&akid=2975%2E251025%2ExgV1uk ]Donate $10 ››

Peter, I’m Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, and I’m running to be Michigan’s
next U.S. senator. I'm a girl dad to two amazing daughters. I've been
married to my wife, Sarah, for 20 years. She's my rock.

[ Abdul's ]Abdul's family.

I was raised by my dad and my stepmom, whose family has called Michigan
home since the 1800s.

Growing up, I never wanted to be a politician. I wanted to be a doctor,
and I became one — earning a PhD and MD.

[ A ]A throwback pic of Abdul graduating.

But in medical school, I realized that the reason why people are sick
usually has a lot less to do with their physiology and more to do with our
politics.

I’m talking about people getting sick because of the air they breathed,
the water they drank, the jobs they worked, the debt they carried. Every
one of those factors is heavily influenced by the actions of our
government.

That's when it clicked. You can't treat your way out of a rigged system.
You have to change it.

So I stopped practicing medicine and started practicing government
instead. We rebuilt Detroit's health department from bankruptcy. We gave
free glasses to thousands of kids who needed them. We launched a program
to erase up to $700 million in medical debt for 200,000 Michiganders. We
proved that our government can be a force for good.

Now, I'm running for the U.S. Senate to take this fight to the next level
and do three simple things:

1. Get corporate money out of politics, so that deep-pocketed interests
don’t get a bigger seat at the table.
2. Put more money in your pockets, so that nobody has to choose between
paying for groceries or rent.
3. Finally pass Medicare for All, so that healthcare is guaranteed from
cradle to grave.

Peter, Mike
Rogers and the MAGA billionaires backing him are spending $51 million
trying to tell you a different story about who I am. But this is the
truth.

[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260820-1-ak.y_M_de&amount=10&refcode=em20260820-2972&t=1006&akid=2975%2E251025%2ExgV1uk ]Chip in $10 or whatever you can today so this
introduction, not some MAGA Super PAC's attack ad, is how Michiganders get
to know me first.

Your friend in the fight,

Abdul

name: Rick | Bennett for Governor
subject: I’m fighting for Maine’s water, woods, and wildlife
disclaimer_text: Paid for and authorized by Bennett for Governor · P
body:
Today along the Androscoggin river I shared my plan to protect our environment and natural resources.

| | |
---
---
---
---
Peter, Today along the Androscoggin river I shared my plan that supports and protects the heart of who we are as Mainers: protecting our environment and natural resources. This is not a side issue, it is a priority. Our clean water, our woods, our wildlife, our working lands, and our coast are part of what makes Maine home. They support our health, our economy, and our way of life. I grew up with a deep respect for this place. My father wrote Maine’s first environmental education curriculum, and I learned early that protecting our natural resources is not just about preserving something beautiful. It is about responsibility. It is about what we leave behind for the next generation. As Governor, I will fight to: #1. Protect clean water and reduce pollution #2. Keep forests intact and habitats connected #3. Build climate resilience in communities across Maine #4. Hold polluters accountable instead of leaving taxpayers with the bill Mainers should not have to choose between a strong economy and a healthy environment. That is a false choice. Protecting Maine’s environment protects Maine jobs. It protects public health. It protects fishing, farming, forestry, tourism, and outdoor recreation. And it protects the Maine way of life that so many of us cherish. For too long, powerful interests have been allowed to create damage while working people and local communities are left to deal with the consequences. I do not accept that. I’m running for Governor because Maine is worth fighting for, and to make sure the next generation can build a life here, too. I need you to help spread this message, support my campaign, and help us fights for Maine’s future.

Darline Graham is worth it. She isn't a career politician. She's the kind of candidate who shows up, tells the truth, and doesn't flinch when things get hard.

She is heading into the final stretch, and the other side knows exactly what's at stake. | | Peter, I ran for office because I persistently witnessed my patients facing impossible choices: **Do I pay for the healthcare I need, or do I pay my rent? Do I buy my prescriptions, or do I put food on the table?** These are not choices any hardworking person should have to make. I’m sounding the alarm because **we are already in a healthcare crisis.** We cannot wait until it gets worse to act. Donald Trump has spent years undermining the public health systems that keep our communities safe and healthy. His Medicaid cuts put community health centers and rural hospitals at much greater risk, threatening access to care for millions of Americans and putting even more strain on an already stretched healthcare workforce. Now, he has launched yet another attack on vaccines, disregarding decades of scientific evidence and the guidance of public health experts. **I know what happens when people cannot afford care. ** We have a chance to change course this November and bring back some stability, protections, experts, and sanity to the House. That’s why I’m honored to be endorsed by healthcare organizations I deeply admire, including Planned Parenthood Action Fund, Care for U.S., and Oregon Nurses Association.

### **NHGOP Thanks Speaker Packard for His Tenure as House Speaker**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** August 20th, 2026
---
| | | **CONTACT** karina@nhrsc.com

---
| |

**CONCORD, N.H.** — Today, NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie issued the following statement as New Hampshire House Speaker Sherman Packard concluded his final session as Speaker of the House:“Yesterday marked Speaker Sherman Packard’s final session leading the New Hampshire House. For the past eight years, Speaker Packard has provided steady leadership through some of the most challenging times in our state’s history, including the COVID-19 pandemic,” said NHGOP Chairman Scott Maltzie. “Under his leadership, New Hampshire continued to build on the advantage that makes our state such a special place to live, work, and raise a family. Speaker Packard has been a dedicated public servant and a strong leader for both the House and the people of New Hampshire.”“While he will not seek another term as Speaker, we are grateful that he will continue his service as a member of the New Hampshire House. On behalf of the NHGOP, I want to thank Speaker Packard for his years of leadership, service, and dedication to our state.”

They are not coming after me — they are coming after YOU

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/GrJDUg1l6WS?e=1facf02470&c2id=205919520b3860dafbe9b9f5dda2019d)
| |
Dear Friend,
In January 2026, investigators received hard evidence of possible election fraud in the 2025 Prop 50 vote.
An audit of Riverside County election materials showed a shocking discrepancy: the Registrar of Voters received 611,428 ballots — yet the certified results reported 657,322 votes.
**That’s 45,896 more votes than ballots received**.
In February, investigators obtained a valid search warrant, signed by a judge, to examine those ballots. The moment it was served, Attorney General Rob Bonta launched pure lawfare.
He raced to Superior Court, then the Court of Appeals — both rejected him — and is now at the California Supreme Court, not to challenge the merits of the investigation, but to shut it down entirely.
This is political corruption and the weaponization of the justice system. Bonta is arguing that he has the power to stop any investigation he doesn’t like — especially one that could expose Democrat election irregularities.
**This is an attack on election integrity**.

Bonta and I will both make our cases before the California Supreme Court on Monday. If he wins, the Court will grant him full authority to halt ANY lawful investigation — including future investigations into himself.
Do not believe the spin from the AG’s office or the media. This is a legal, judge-approved investigation into possible election fraud that Bonta desperately wants stopped.
We must all ask ourselves why.
Make no mistake: **they are not coming after me — they are coming after YOU**.
They are coming after anyone who defends the rule of law. They want to make an example of this case so no sheriff, no investigator, and no patriot ever dares look under the hood of California’s elections again.
**We cannot let them win.**
Rob Bonta and his Democrat lawyers have already spent $250,000 of your tax dollars trying to silence this investigation — and they plan to spend millions more.
I am humbly asking for your support to defeat Bonta in court.
**Please contribute today to help us fight back.**
Thank you,
