name: Swing Left
subject: We must restore Minnesota's Democratic trifecta
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Swing Left, [swingleft
body:
Minnesota Dems last secured a trifecta in 2022.
#
Hi there,
This year, to fight back against Republican gerrymandering and voter suppression, a key part of our long-term strategy, we need to win in the states. Swing Left has identified the most competitive races that will determine the balance of state-level power—and Minnesota is one of our most important opportunities in this fight.
Minnesota Democrats secured a trifecta in 2022, and in 2023 they delivered one of the most transformative, pro-worker legislative packages in modern state history. They passed guaranteed paid family and medical leave, secured earned paid sick days, and enacted safety protections for warehouse and meatpacking workers. They proved exactly what is possible when Democrats have full governing power.
[](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-mn-2026.2iUXYB&refcode=em20260820-2518&t=1&akid=2518%2E1562180%2EX4Upjz) | [](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-mn-2026.2iUXYB&refcode=em20260820-2518&t=2&akid=2518%2E1562180%2EX4Upjz)
---|---
However, that progress was stumped when the trifecta was broken in 2024. Now the State House is an exact 67-67 split, and the parties enacted a power-sharing deal that handed Republicans control of the chamber in exchange for the official seating of Democratic Rep. Brad Tabke. Today, Democrats defend a single-seat majority in the State Senate while fighting to reclaim the House.
Now, we have a clear chance to win a trifecta in Minnesota. With **Democratic U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar** favored to succeed Governor Tim Walz, if we hold Democrats’ narrow majority in the State Senate and flip the State House back to a Democratic majority, we can help restore full Democratic control in the state.
Control of both chambers will be decided by a handful of ultra-competitive toss-up districts, which is why we’re directing grassroots funds straight to Minnesota’s Democratic legislative campaign committees, ensuring every dollar goes directly to the high-stakes races that will determine majority control.
**[If you are ready to help us hold the State Senate, flip the State House, and restore Minnesota’s Democratic trifecta, will you make a donation of $25 to our Minnesota Win in the States Fund today?](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-mn-2026.2iUXYB&refcode=em20260820-2518&amount=25&t=3&akid=2518%2E1562180%2EX4Upjz)**
**[Donate $25 Now](https://act.swingleft.org/go/27?c0=sl-states-mn-2026.2iUXYB&refcode=em20260820-2518&amount=25&t=4&akid=2518%2E1562180%2EX4Upjz)**
Thank you for being part of this work.
— The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. [**If you’d like to help support our work, you can make a donation using this link.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em_ms_sl_footer?refcode=em20260820-1&t=5&refcode2=2518_1562180_X4Upjz&akid=2518%2E1562180%2EX4Upjz)

subject: Unbought and unbossed

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

Did you happen to catch our Communications Director, Usamah Andrabi, on
Zeteo’s Mehdi Unfiltered this week?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260820.ikp0LD&refcode=em20260820-38181&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38181%2E1203867%2EysSQVm ]Headline: "Is a New, Expanded Progressive 'Squad' Coming to Congress in
2027?: Justice Democrats' Usamah Andrabi discusses the recent primary
upsets, his left-wing organization's relationship with the DSA, and how
Dem candidates have successfully stood up to corporate PAC money.";
attached is image of Mehdi Hasan (left) and Usamah Andrabi (right)
speaking to each other at a table

Usamah sat down with Mehdi Hasan to talk about the big wins for Justice
Democrats and the progressive movement at large this year. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260820.ikp0LD&refcode=em20260820-38181&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38181%2E1203867%2EysSQVm ]Before we
get into it, will you pitch in any amount to fuel our general election
fights?

As Mehdi pointed out, more than half of the 15 primary candidates we
endorsed won, and we still have three more general election races in
November. When asked how we decided who to endorse and where, Usamah
explained that the key to our success in these primaries is candidate
recruitment and community outreach.

Every cycle, JD looks at congressional districts — often deep blue
districts represented by corporate shills, AIPAC-backed incumbents, or
Crypto billionaires. We then talk to people on the ground and ask if
they’re being served well enough by their representative, and too often
the answer is no. Our next question is: who do they think could be a
better leader to serve their community?

That’s how we recruited New York’s Darializa Avila Chevalier and Detroit’s
Donavan McKinney to run, and secured additional primary wins in New
Jersey, Pennsylvania, Colorado, and Texas.

One major takeaway from these victories? Voters are ready to move on from
the failed establishment. Overwhelmingly, Democratic voters don’t want to
see their taxpayer dollars spent on endless wars and genocide abroad, and
yet, only a minority of Democrats in Congress represent that view.

At the heart of it, “The Democratic base is excited by our candidates
because they are showing you don’t have to be bought and sold to be
leaders for your communities. In fact, you can’t be leaders for your
community unless you are unbought and unbossed.”

Because we don’t take a cent from corporate PACs, our ability to recruit
and financially support candidates is fueled entirely by grassroots
donations from people like you. Now, we’re sending at least 7 new Justice
Democrats to Congress next year, and we can make that 10 if we come
together and win in the general election.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260820.ikp0LD&refcode=em20260820-38181&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=38181%2E1203867%2EysSQVm ]So Peter,
can we count on you to chip in $5 or more to keep the 2026
wins coming for JD and our progressive movement?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260820.ikp0LD&refcode=em20260820-38181&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=38181%2E1203867%2EysSQVm ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

When I was a kid, good service meant that you walked into a place and somebody smiled, greeted you, talked to you, and helped you through the process of purchasing or deciding what you wanted. Maybe they even did a little something extra, like carrying your bags to the car or wrapping something for you free of charge because, hey, they wanted your business.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4dfd9970-8203-4b86-8012-29ef281bf8f3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The people working there had in-depth knowledge of the products they sold or the skills they provided. You felt confident that you were going to get exactly what you wanted. Customization and talking through decisions were expected.
"Service with a smile," as they used to say.
"The customer is always right."
Those little things helped small businesses and even major corporations succeed and gain loyal customers. It was something we all understood.
More and more, my friends and I find ourselves asking the same question: What the hell happened to service?
* * *
## We Don't Get Service Anymore
Maybe this is another lament from a middle-aged man, but it is a common theme among my friends in their 30s, 40s, and 50s. Service is not the same.
Customer-service calls have been exported to call centers. You press one for English and two for Español. Then you hear the familiar recording: "Please listen carefully because our menu options have recently changed."
You spend the next five minutes trying to determine whether you should press four for sales, five for office hours, or repeatedly smash zero while screaming, "Representative," into your phone.
Then there is restaurant service. A 20% tip used to represent great service that exceeded expectations. Now, 20% feels like the standard, almost mandatory amount because we have been guilted into accepting that this is simply how workers get paid.
You do not even need to receive actual service anymore. Someone spins a computer screen around and passively says, "The screen is going to ask you a few questions," as if neither of you knows what the question will be.
Money, please.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/cdb80204-0df1-415f-8d81-76fcf99852a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The strange part is that this may be one of the only times you will hear me say this with "complete confidence:" **I may be getting old.**
And I am starting to wonder whether the idea of good service has fundamentally changed.
* * *
## What If We Are the Ones Who Don't Understand?...

_**Cliff 's Note: **_
##### **I don't endorse folks who aren't Democrats. That's not a thing I usually do. I'm doing it anyway. Seth Bodnar. Green Beret. Iraq, 2003. Ran the University of Montana for eight years.**
##### **Won't caucus with either party if he gets there.**
##### **I asked him about Hegseth's loyalty tests inside the Pentagon. He said: "That's not what I fought for. That's not what my friends died for."**
##### **That's when I decided. Vote Bodnar in Montana.**
[ Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Fe-4SnbRdJBCh0vdJFXbo5eB2EGTShLx1GwLAO92ljw?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=212020813)
_**-- Cliff**_
* * *
Cliff sat down with Seth Bodnar for a special edition of _Amped Up_ , and the moment that landed hardest had nothing to do with polling. Bodnar--West Point graduate, Green Beret, infantry platoon leader in Iraq in 2003, and for eight years president of the University of Montana--described stacking up against a wall outside a suspected safe house in the middle of the night, and the one question that never came up: what party are you a part of.
He carried that straight to Pete Hegseth's loyalty tests inside the Pentagon and refused to soften it. "That's not patriotic. That's not what I fought for. That's not what my friends died for." The same argument runs through his answer on Iran, where he says Congress has abdicated its constitutional war powers out of blind partisan loyalty, and that abdication is precisely how you lose a war.
The rest is economic populism with a Montana accent. The politics are the part progressives will argue about: he won't caucus with either party, he wants a bloc of independent-minded senators instead, and he says Montana deserves a senator who doesn't work for Chuck Schumer and isn't afraid of Donald Trump. Jon Tester, Max Baucus, two former state Democratic Party chairs, a former Republican governor, and the former Montana GOP chair have all lined up behind him. By the end of the interview, so had Cliff.

Dear Friend,
I want you to stand at that voting counter with me. Minneapolis. Primary day. **[I lean in and ask the election judge one question:](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-JQ/s7mea40918d)** **how many people am I allowed to vouch for?** [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-JQ/s7mea40918d) **
"Eight."** **Not one. EIGHT.** So I tell her exactly what she is agreeing to. **These people are not registered. They have no ID. No license, no bill, no paperwork of any kind.** She does not blink. She does not hesitate. She says: **"You are the ID."** I said it back to her, just to be sure I had heard it right. **_I am the ID._** She agreed. [**Help me tear this open.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.-JQ/s7mea40918d) That single sentence is the entire wall standing between a legitimate election and a fraudulent one. Not a database, not a document, not a verification of any kind. **One man's word, accepted at the counter.** Now let me show you how deep this particular hole actually goes, because every single thing I am about to tell you makes the thing before it considerably worse. **EIGHT.** Minnesota law permits one registered voter to swear an oath that eight other people live in his precinct, and on the strength of that oath alone those eight individuals register on the spot and vote that same day. **Not one piece of documentation ever changes hands.** **UNLIMITED.** Then you read the sentence that comes immediately after it: "This limitation does not apply to an employee of a residential facility." If you happen to work at a nursing home, the eight-person cap disappears entirely. **There is no number written anywhere. There is no ceiling at all.** **NOBODY WRITES IT DOWN.** Scott Pressler's team requested a list of the people who had been vouched in from four different Minnesota cities: Minneapolis, St. Paul, Duluth and St. Cloud. **All four came back with nothing whatsoever, because that list does not exist anywhere in the state.** An election worker circles a number on a form, and that circled number is the entire permanent record. In Dimock, just 35 miles from Fern’s home, she’s seen residents deal with water contamination so severe that some can still light their tap water on fire. Fern’s first priority is regulating the rapid expansion of AI data centers. From coal mining to fracking, she’s seen how promises of economic development can leave Pennsylvanians dealing with degraded ecosystems and air quality hazards. She worked alongside NEPA community members to develop a data center land use ordinance for her own township. In office, Fern plans to: ✅ Support a moratorium on data centers ✅ Protect Pennsylvanians’ right to clean water and affordable utilities ✅ Expand access to community solar while environmentally remediating mining sites ✅ And hold corporations and polluters financially accountable for their actions. | This is our chance to flip District 120 blue – for a future that works for all NEPA residents, not just the wealthy utilities. | | | | | | Hello Peter,
I have some very encouraging news to share:
**Our latest polling shows our campaign 6.3 percentage points ahead of our Republican opponent.**
That tells us something important: **we have a real opportunity to win this race and flip Ohio's 8th Congressional District.**
But a polling lead is not a victory — and **we cannot assume we will hold that lead without the resources to compete.**
Last week, our campaign received **250 yard signs and 10,000 pieces of campaign literature.**
**We are already out.**
Think about that for a moment.
In just five days, supporters and volunteers moved **250 signs and 10,000 pieces of literature** into communities across the district. Our volunteers are canvassing. Supporters are requesting signs. Voters are learning about this campaign.
**The demand is there. Now we have to keep up with it.**

### We need your help to protect this 6.3-point lead.

Our opponent will have the resources to communicate with voters through Election Day. We have to be able to do the same.
We urgently need funding for:
* **Thousands more pieces of campaign literature** for canvassing and lit drops
* **Hundreds more yard signs** to meet supporter requests
* **Large roadside signs** in high-visibility locations
* **Digital advertising and voter outreach**
* **The field operation necessary to turn supporters into voters**

If we cannot afford to replenish our literature, purchase signs, advertise, and continue reaching voters, **our opponent has an opportunity to close that 6.3-point gap.** We cannot let that happen.

### This is a race we can win.

We aren't asking you to invest in a campaign with no path to victory.**We're asking you to help us protect a lead.**
[A contribution of **$25** helps us print more voter literature.](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=900a157b7e&e=c6e7dff14c)[**$50 or $100** helps put more signs and campaign materials into neighborhoods.](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=d493065f05&e=c6e7dff14c)[And contributions of **$250, $500, or more** give us the ability to dramatically expand our voter-contact and advertising efforts.](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=0311b982d9&e=c6e7dff14c)
**Please donate today:**
[ https://enochforcongress.com/donate-now](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=eff32b1eb4&e=c6e7dff14c)
If you've already contributed, **thank you.** Your support helped put us in this position. But I'm asking you to consider giving again because this campaign has reached a critical moment.
**Being 6.3 points ahead means we have an opportunity. It does not guarantee a victory.**
We have to turn that polling advantage into actual votes.That means knocking on more doors.Putting more literature into voters' hands.Putting more signs in neighborhoods.Running more digital ads.Recruiting more volunteers.
And making sure voters throughout OH-8 know that **they have a real choice in this election.**

### We have the momentum. Now we need the resources to sustain it.

**10,000 pieces of literature — gone.****250 signs — gone.****+6.3 points in the polls.**
Now we need to **restock, expand, and keep pushing all the way to Election Day.**
**Donate today:**
[ https://enochforcongress.com/donate-now](https://enochforcongress.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=488c703b71891f0b712737c99&id=73d2216a31&e=c6e7dff14c)
Together, we can protect this lead, win this election, and **flip Ohio's 8th Congressional District.**
Thank you for standing with me.
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**

Ohio's 8th Congressional District

body:
Hey there, I’m sorry to reach out again

Hey there, I know my team has been reaching out a lot lately, and I hate to pile on — but I’m throwing a Hail Mary here. I just took a look at our fundraising numbers for the month so far, and unless we see a big boost in donations from your area, we’re at _severe_ risk of falling short of our August projections. [_**So I have to ask: will you rush a donation, and begin your support for this campaign?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137619868/641375673/1480016760?amounts=5,10,25,50,100,250,500&refcode=email_082026_hailmary-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMDk5MTRjYy1lNzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SRWEKw7R-pVS4Mcjt8MDI7gW4GuJhHGIJqN8VhGp_xQ=) | | [Donate →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137619869/641375674/1480016760?amounts=5,10,25,50,100,250,500&refcode=email_082026_hailmary-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMDk5MTRjYy1lNzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SRWEKw7R-pVS4Mcjt8MDI7gW4GuJhHGIJqN8VhGp_xQ=)
---
Here’s the thing: Falling short of _some_ fundraising goals isn’t the end of the world. I’ve seen what this grassroots team is able to accomplish, and I have faith in our ability to recover from tough setbacks.
But Election Day is only getting closer, and the stakes are only getting higher.
I’ve said it once, and I’ll say it again: [**The road to flipping the House blue runs through OR-06.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137619870/641375675/1480016760?refcode=email_082026_hailmary-RS&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzEvMS85Mzg4OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmMDk5MTRjYy1lNzljLWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=SRWEKw7R-pVS4Mcjt8MDI7gW4GuJhHGIJqN8VhGp_xQ=)
If we don’t defend this seat, that means two more years of unchecked Republican rule, two more years of higher costs, and two more years of leadership that puts politics and their wallets above working families.

* * *
With only 3 months left until the midterms, Democrats have been screaming at the top of their lungs: "Affordability, affordability, affordability."
Now, obviously affordability is important. In fact, polls show that the economy is always the #1 issue. But Democrats are pushing the narrative that under Trump, prices have gotten worse.
I want to show you 4 graphs that completely refute that...
And the third one is personal for me:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/80548803-8a4e-4fe8-87d7-2b37a3f8210a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Rent is actually down.
The housing crisis has been very real since COVID stifled supply, and interest rates soared, driven by Bidenflation in the early 2020s. Against all odds, Trump is reversing that.
In early 2021, the U.S. monthly national rent saw an 18.2% YoY change, one of the largest increases in U.S. history. Prices continued to go up, though to a smaller degree, until Biden completed his time in office.
Then, something extraordinary happened. Rent didn't just go up at a slower rate; it actually dropped in price.

* * *
**[Together with Hear.com](https://substack.com/redirect/4687535d-9ed6-4629-87c9-6aa9cf72f908?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
# **Audiologists Are Raving About This Nearly Invisible Hearing Aid**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4687535d-9ed6-4629-87c9-6aa9cf72f908?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Nearly invisible yet powerful in noisy places. Its secret? A German-engineered dual-processing chips that separates speech from noise in real time.
**[See for yourself with a 45 day, no risk trial.](https://substack.com/redirect/4687535d-9ed6-4629-87c9-6aa9cf72f908?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Experience Clarity](https://substack.com/redirect/4687535d-9ed6-4629-87c9-6aa9cf72f908?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
_**(Piece continues)**_
At no point in the Trump presidency has rent gone up in price, and currently, rent prices are decreasing at a rate of 1.1% year over year.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8267709f-52c3-40c5-b628-f6c2c610efb3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Groceries have undeniably gone up. Inflation, oil prices, and supply chain problems have led to a sharp price increase in goods like orange juice and beef.
But what many don't know is that the price of eggs is down 30%. Bacon, chicken, and bread have seen hardly any increase in the past year.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3d8b0790-c0e2-4274-9a32-dcde9d1f1f3e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This is one of the most impactful Trump policies for me. With the implementation of TrumpRX and new negotiations with the pharmaceutical industry, Trump has decreased pharmaceutical prices more than any other president since the 1960s.
Year over year, prescription drugs are down 3.1%, while they were up nearly 5% YoY under Biden.
One year ago this month, I was diagnosed with Type 1 diabetes. Type 1 diabetes requires multiple medications, medical devices, and, of course, insulin. Trump's free-market approach to pharmaceuticals has saved me and my family hundreds of dollars, and done what socialist Democrats said was impossible.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e5627dfc-66a4-4044-842a-9603e92d1ede?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The reality is, free-market policies and common-sense problem solving works. Democrats openly oppose what Trump has accomplished.
58% of Democrats view socialism positively, and half view capitalism negatively. The terrifying reality is that if Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress, they would rapidly implement policies that reverse Trump's progress.
...
One honorable mention for Trump: Although gas is currently high due to the Iran war, gas prices on average are still lower than during the Biden administration.
None of this is to say that the prices of goods are as they should be. It isn't to say that things are easy or that families aren't struggling. It simply refutes the idea that Trump doesn't have things trending in the right direction. And implementing socialism will only get us back into the problems that started this mess in the first place.

| | | | | **2026 August e-newsletter**

* Caltrain at a Critical Crossroads
* Celebrating a New Gateway to San Bruno Mountain
* Building Age-Friendly Communities for Every Generation

| | |
---

# “As wildfires rage across the state, nation and world and with a heat wave arriving, now is the time to prepare your families and communities how to be prepared to minimize the risk"
# **\- Supervisor David Canepa**
---
| | | | **2026 August e-newsletter** **Building Age-Friendly Communities for Every Generation** Dear friends, Nearly a decade ago, I helped launch an effort based on a simple idea: San Mateo County should be a place where people can age with dignity, independence and connection. That vision has grown into one of the most successful countywide Age-Friendly initiatives in California. With an initial Measure K investment, and approximately $1 million in total County Measure K support over the years, the Center for Age-Friendly Excellence, or CAFE, has helped transform how our cities plan for a rapidly aging population. Since July 2018, CAFE has supported 14 San Mateo County cities in becoming certified and joining AARP’s Network of Age-Friendly States and Communities, while developing eight local action plans to help communities become more livable for people of all ages. CAFE's work goes beyond a designation. It brings residents, local governments, nonprofits and community partners together to examine transportation, housing, accessibility, social connection, health and other issues that affect our quality of life. Its mission is to improve the health, well-being and quality of life of older adults and people with disabilities through community-driven planning, direct services and cross-sector collaboration. Today, the Age-Friendly movement is also an important part of our broader effort to combat isolation and loneliness and build stronger connections between neighbors and generations. The County’s Measure K investments have supported seniors, people with disabilities and other residents through programs designed to improve quality of life. I am proud that an idea we began nearly a decade ago has grown into a countywide movement. As San Mateo County ages, we must continue planning not just for longer lives, but for better lives, where residents can remain active, connected and engaged in the communities they call home. See a video on an Age-Friendly workshop in Brisbane here: **[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5rnJ7Mp6xo8&list=PLceI4wCiqVySkfQ4tEAbhaEAjZ_tu5ktL&index=1](https://us.list-manage.com/11xdxJgDuXv?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02 "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5rnJ7Mp6xo8&list=PLceI4wCiqVySkfQ4tEAbhaEAjZ_tu5ktL&index=1")** ** ** **Celebrating a New Gateway to San Bruno Mountain** I was proud to join our community in celebrating the ribbon cutting of the new Day Use Improvement Project and Interpretive Center at San Bruno Mountain County and State Park. San Bruno Mountain is one of San Mateo County’s great natural treasures, a place where families, students, hikers and visitors can experience the outdoors, take in spectacular views and learn about the unique ecosystems that make this mountain so special. I was pleased to secure $2 million in Measure K funding to help get this important project off the ground. Those dollars have been transformed into a more welcoming, accessible and educational space for everyone who visits. The improvements include a new interpretive pavilion and gathering space, educational displays, nearly two dozen new picnic tables and BBQ grills, and a larger restroom facility with four all-gender, ADA-accessible restrooms, sinks and changing tables. Six of the park’s nine new picnic sites are fully accessible, and a circular paved pathway connects the sites, making it easier for people of all abilities to enjoy the park. The project was also shaped by community input gathered through surveys in 2022 and 2023, ensuring these improvements reflect the needs and priorities of the people who use and love San Bruno Mountain. This is about more than new buildings and picnic tables. It is about creating a place where people can gather, learn about our local environment and build connections with one another and the outdoors. I am incredibly proud of this investment and grateful to San Mateo County Parks, the community and everyone who helped bring this vision to life. I encourage everyone to visit San Bruno Mountain and experience this beautiful new space for themselves. The above photo is courtesy of San Mateo County Parks Ranger Rob Cala. See an NBC report on the ribbon cutting here: [https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/upgrades-san-bruno-mountain-state-county-park/4084171/](https://us.list-manage.com/onl2LjbydFv?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02 "https://www.nbcbayarea.com/news/local/upgrades-san-bruno-mountain-state-county-park/4084171/") **Caltrain at a Critical Crossroads** Caltrain is one of the Peninsula’s greatest transportation assets, but it is approaching a serious fiscal cliff that could have major consequences for San Mateo County residents. The concern is especially striking because Caltrain is succeeding. Ridership is growing, customer satisfaction is strong, and the new electrified system is providing faster, cleaner and more reliable service. Yet without a stable, long-term source of funding, Caltrain could face an annual operating deficit of approximately $75 million and potentially significant service reductions in the coming years. The consequences could be dramatic: The elimination of weekend service, trains running only once an hour, station closures, earlier service endings and fewer transportation options for families, workers, students and seniors. That would mean more cars on Highway 101, more traffic and more pollution. It would also undermine the tremendous public investment already made to modernize and electrify this critical rail system. As a Caltrain Board member, I believe maintaining a strong transit system is an investment in our environment, economy and quality of life. Every person who chooses the train instead of driving helps reduce congestion and greenhouse gas emissions. Caltrain also connects people to jobs, schools, businesses and communities throughout the Peninsula. In November, voters will have a choice regarding whether to provide dedicated funding for Caltrain's future. That decision comes at an important moment for the railroad and the communities it serves. The question is not whether Caltrain matters, it clearly does. The challenge before us is how we ensure that this vital public asset has the financial stability necessary to continue serving future generations.

**Step Back in Time at Rancho Day Fiesta** Families can step back into California’s rancho era at the annual Rancho Day Fiesta, a free, family-friendly event hosted by the San Mateo County Historical Association at the historic Sánchez Adobe in Pacifica. Visitors will travel back to the 1840s, when Don Francisco Sanchez raised cattle at Rancho San Pedro, and experience history through hands-on activities. Kids and adults can make adobe bricks, stamp leather, dip candles, create corn husk dolls and churn butter. Guests can also learn how early Californios danced and discover what daily life was like during the rancho period. The event is a wonderful opportunity for families to experience local history in a fun, interactive way and admission is free. The Sánchez Adobe is a unique piece of San Mateo County’s history and a great place to introduce young people to our region’s past. **Date:** Saturday, September 19
**Time:** Noon–4 p.m.
**Address:** Sánchez Adobe, 1000 Linda Mar Blvd., Pacifica
**More information:** [San Mateo County Historical Association](https://us.list-manage.com/13ZnzaomGAp?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02 "https://www.historysmc.org?utm_source=chatgpt.com")
In friendship,
**DAVID J. CANEPA**
San Mateo County Board of Supervisors

Denton County is one of the fastest growing parts of Texas, but it hasn't elected a Democrat to the Commissioner's Court in 40 years. It’s also a must-win for James Talarico in this year’s U.S. Senate race.
**That’s why we’re so excited that Candace Valenzuela is running for County Commissioner. Her victory means real representation in north Texas _and_ it gives Talarico a fighting chance to become the next senator from Texas.**
Denton has quickly shifted from a reliably red county to a true battleground, and Candace is at the forefront of that change. For example, more than 20,000 Democrats voted in the March primary, which is 1,800 more than voted on the Republican side.
And she's beaten the odds before, defeating an 18-year incumbent for a seat on the local School Board, where she delivered for students and families. Now she's bringing that same fight to Denton County.
_The momentum behind her is real, and so is her chance to deliver for Denton County and the full Democratic ticket._
**Candace is the key to winning statewide.** Her street-level campaign will turnout voters that the campaigns for senate and governor won’t be able to reach. That's why Powered by People is going all in for Candace and doing the work alongside her to bring in young Texans, first-time voters, rural communities and others that often get left behind.

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

subject: the threats to our outdoors won’t go unanswered
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/134?t=1&akid=11895%2E400544%2EGYSrDf)
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16194?t=2&akid=11895%2E400544%2EGYSrDf)
Friend, some of my earliest memories are of being outside with my dad.

My dad grew up on a farm and passed his love of the outdoors on to us. I remember running through the desert with my cousins and fishing with my dad. Those experiences taught me from a young age that we all have a responsibility to care for the places we call home.
_But Trump and his administration are threatening the very places that make New Mexico special._
Right now, our sacred land, clear water, and clean air are under attack. The Trump administration is moving to slash protections for sacred lands, including the lands surrounding Chaco Canyon and Bears Ears, and reopen them to mining and oil and gas drilling. You might have even seen the photos of construction crews bulldozing Big Bend National Park for Trump’s border wall.
**I’m running for Governor to put our environment over profit and to stand up to anyone who dares attack our beautiful state.[_If you’re with me, your support today would make a huge difference in this campaign to protect New Mexico’s environment._](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/16194?t=3&akid=11895%2E400544%2EGYSrDf)**
